Subject: Renewal planning: sudden steady spikes + request for short buffer

Hi Mina,

Quick note ahead of our renewal conversation later this month. Over the last 6 weeks we've seen repeated short-lived peaks in inference throughput that cross our provisioned capacity and trigger throttles for internal workflows (mostly low-latency conversational routing). I've attached the Q3 utilization extract.

Numbers in brief: sustained 90th pct token-rate spikes that last anywhere from 2–18 minutes daily, and several longer sessions last week that pushed utilization to ~98% for 45–90 minutes.

We have three asks up-front:
- Can Redwood provide a short-term buffer (extra GPUs) to smooth those peaks while we finalize our model caching changes?
- If we add buffer capacity, can that be scoped as an interim tranche in the renewal (so it auto-rolls into the renewal commitment if used)?
- Can we propose a staged plan to reprofile the commit after 6–8 weeks based on actual utilization post-buffering?

We'd prefer minimal change to our network connectivity; just want predictable availability while we ship a caching improvement.

Attachments: novamed_q3_utilization.csv (summary)

Thanks,
Elaine Cho
Head of Platform Ops
Novamed AI

Hi Elaine — thanks for the data and the clear asks.

Short answer: yes, we can. We have two practical paths I recommend depending on how aggressive you want to be on spend vs. risk:

Option A (conservative, low immediate cost):
- Add a 6-GPU buffer pool attached to your Dedicated fleet for 30 days.
- Monitor 1:1 with your team; if utilization continues to require it after 30 days, convert the buffer into a transient tranche (counts toward renewal commitments) or extend month-to-month.

Option B (smoother outcome for bursts):
- Add an 8-GPU burst buffer + enable automatic prefix/KV caching changes we can deploy as a canary.
- Reprofile after 6 weeks and move to a stepped ramp (e.g., keep 6 GPUs steady, scale remaining 2 up only during scheduled windows).

Operational notes:
- We can configure autoscale rules to keep the buffer cold-cost minimized (sleep VMs + warm GPU pool).
- We can also apply an interim credit for months where average utilization is below the committed baseline — happy to model that in the renewal doc.

Next steps I suggest: I will loop Ben (Sales Ops) and Marcus (Solutions) to get a quick capacity & pricing model and a proposed schedule. If you can confirm whether you prefer Option A or B (or we can pick a hybrid), I’ll produce a proposed change order and a DocuSign link.

Proposed immediate action items:
- Elaine: indicate preference (A/B/hybrid) and any blackout windows for deployment.
- Ben: provide pricing and tranche wording.
- Marcus: run an initial fit-check on 6 vs 8 GPUs for the current workload shape.

Thanks — I’ll aim to have a draft change order by EOD Tues.

Best,

Analysis summary (from our utilization model):
- Baseline committed GPU usage (Q3 moving average) = 42 GPUs consumed 24/7.
- Daily short spikes push burst consumption to 54–58 GPUs but are typically < 20 mins; large sustained events last ~60–90 mins and drove the recent throttles.
- Probability of >90% sustained utilization in next 30 days (without buffer) = ~0.28.

Recommendation (price + ops trade-off):
- Immediate: provision 6 GPUs now (fastest time to safety).
- Week 6: review telemetry; if >70% of spikes are still resulting in service-level impact, add 4 GPUs (bringing steady state to +10).
- Offer: one month pro-rated credit if Novamed converts the 6-GPU buffer into committed capacity at renewal.

I attached a simple pricing calc and suggested commit wording. Also added a suggested runbook: tagging, FIFO burst routing, and TTL for prefix caches to lower token-costs during peaks.

Let me know and I’ll generate the change order and push the DocuSign link.
